title: Young People who Leave Education System after Major Examinations
what_it_is: Young People who Leave Education System after Major Examinations

sections.label: Primary 1 cohort progression
sections.summary: Nearly all P1 cohorts progress to secondary, under 1% do not complete secondary, and 97% now reach post-secondary education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With all these measures, the proportion of Primary 1 (P1) cohorts who did not progress to Secondary education is practically 0%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At the Secondary school level, less than 1% of the P1 cohorts did not complete Secondary education, compared to 2% 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The percentage of P1 cohorts that progresses to post-Secondary education has increased from 90% 10 years ago, to 97% now.

sections.label: MOE dropout tracking
sections.summary: MOE does not track school dropouts statistically and longitudinally as a group because different agencies provide support at different life stages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOE does not track students who drop out of schools statistically and longitudinally as a group because different agencies and organisations do come in to provide support at different stages of a person’s life.

sections.label: Re-admission to formal education
sections.summary: The formal education system welcomes back dropouts, and working experience will now be considered when assessing re-admission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, our formal education system, whether it is Institute of Technical Education, polytechnic, university, if you drop out for some reason, it will welcome you back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Member may notice that, last week, I announced that we will now also take into account their working experience when we assess re-admission.

sections.label: Lifelong learning enrolment
sections.summary: Enrolment for a lifelong learning programme should not require certain academic grades, and it is subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: You should not have to demonstrate that you have achieved certain academic grades in order to enrol for a lifelong learning programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So long as you have the heart, the determination to do it, it should welcome you and it is also subsidised.
